One of the most surprising findings from our latest research wasn't about AI, budgets, or buying intent. It was how quickly leadership turnover makes CRM data obsolete.

Across the UK, France, and Germany, the average CMO now spends less than 29 months in role. CROs average around 31 months. Even CEOs average under four years.

The result? Half of a company's C-suite CRM data becomes inaccurate in less than two years. 

We often talk about accuracy as a snapshot. But the real challenge is freshness. A contact record can be perfectly accurate today and completely useless tomorrow if the person has moved roles, changed responsibilities, or left the business entirely.

document.title: How well do you know your CRM?

posts.content:
Most CRM audits end in a spreadsheet nobody opens again. 


So we've put together this step-by-step guide that gives you a handy to-do list by the end.

 1. Pick one high-value segment – not the whole CRM
 2. Check completeness on the fields that matter (email, phone, job title, seniority)
 3. Check freshness – because complete doesn't always mean current
 4. Check source attribution – every lead needs a clear origin
 5. Find duplicates and decide what "most trusted" means
 6. Compare across teams, regions and sources – the gaps usually cluster
 7. Prioritise fixes by revenue impact, not by what's easiest

Do this on a sample of 50-100 records and find out where your data is bleeding pipeline. 

With 1 in 3 contacts changing every year, it's no wonder a one-off clean-up only buys you a few good months.

Want to understand how to maintain data that's always ready to act on? Check out our article in the comments.

#CRM #B2Bcontactdata #dataenrichment
